title: Route Surface & Road Type Finder
description: Inspect OpenStreetMap surface and road-type tags on ways near a driving route; counts are not route distances.
summary_sentence: Nearby mapped roads can have different surface tags from the actual route. Verify the route and current conditions before travel.
quick_answer: The tool routes a drive and counts OpenStreetMap ways within 30 metres of up to 20 sampled route points. Nearby ways can be off the route; counts are not distance shares. Elevation gain is sampled when available.
steps_intro: Enter a start and destination, then inspect nearby map tags as preliminary context:

Mapped surface tags may be incomplete or out of date. Check current route conditions with local sources before touring.
Counts of nearby ways do not establish whether a route is suitable or accessible for a vehicle. Check local restrictions and conditions.
Compare nearby mapped tags cautiously: counts are neither route length nor proof of the surface on the selected road.

body.t: A gravel-tagged way within 30 metres of a sampled point may be a parallel road. Its presence in the count does not prove the routed road is gravel.
Ways without an OpenStreetMap surface tag are counted as not recorded. Missing data should not be treated as a paved or unpaved classification.

faq: What if a road has no surface recorded?
A returned nearby way without a surface tag is counted as not recorded. The counts are not percentages of the route.
How is the sampling done?

The tool samples up to 20 points along the driving route and requests OSM highway ways within 30 metres, up to 400 returned ways. These can include ways not on the route; counts are by way, not distance.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Surfaces change with seasons and works, not with traffic.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
The route sampled is the road route — surfaces belong to roads, not to crow lines.
Can route results change over time?
Yes, happily: OpenStreetMap's surface coverage improves as mappers record more roads. A re-run next season can shrink the unknown share.
Does it show elevation too?
When the elevation service is available, it estimates gain from sampled elevations along the route. Sampling may miss changes between points.
Can it force a gravel-only or paved-only route?
No. It uses a driving route and does not constrain routing by surface.
Can it tell me a road is closed?
No — surfaces and types, not closures. A mapped gravel road may still be gated; local signs outrank data.
Why does my route show 100% unknown?
The tool reports counts, not percentages. Returned ways without a surface tag are shown as not recorded.
Cobblestone counts as paved?
The tool displays the recorded surface value rather than assigning it to a paved or unpaved category.
